clue.text: Bounce around with fondness for housework

parts.note: to bounce is to spring up
C is short for circa, Latin for around
a leaning is a liking or fondness

explanation.surface: Someone bounces about the house, plainly enjoying the chores.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorough annual clean of a home is a standard name for a burst of housework.

clue.text: Head of State with stomach nearly drained is very thin

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a craw is a bird's crop, loosely the stomach

indicators.note: a word drained of its contents keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A national leader whose belly has been almost emptied looks gaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawny describes someone bony and lean, a synonym for very thin.

clue.text: Stones legendary bird adjacent to outskirts of kennels

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Rocks found beside a mythical bird near the edge of some dog kennels.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones and rocks are synonyms for lumps of mineral matter.

clue.text: Woodland deity retreats south and sleeps

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the deity's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of woods and shepherds, who appears in The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A forest god withdraws southwards and dozes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Naps are short sleeps, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: See 1
Played right in middle of mere and died

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for mere

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: Someone played about in the middle of a lake and drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark is to fool about or play mischievously.

clue.text: Twitch follows fractured tibia, on medication

indicators.note: the twitch comes after the other letters
broken bones suggest letters broken and rearranged

parts.note: a tic is a twitch

explanation.surface: A patient with a broken shin develops a twitch while on medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word but belongs to the fodder that 'fractured' scrambles; 'follows' puts the twitch last.
explanation.definitionFit: An antibiotic is a drug for bacterial infection, a kind of medication.

clue.text: Cod line disentangled from top of cap

indicators.note: the line letter is freed from the front of the word for cap

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit, a limitation

explanation.surface: An angler untangles fishing line from a cod caught on the top of a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' is the fish in the surface but means fake or sham here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective means mock or sham, so it describes an imitation.

clue.text: Secure 1 Across and improve health

parts.note: to secure something is to get it
the answer at 1 Across begins with a word meaning a spring of water, which is also a well

explanation.surface: Fix a spring clean and you'll feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference uses only the first word of 1 Across, a water spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is the meaning of the phrase, which means regain strength after illness.

clue.text: Mushroom article featuring in older cookery sheets?

indicators.note: these letters appear inside the word for older

parts.note: riper means more mature, older
a cep is a kind of edible mushroom
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old cookbook features a mushroom article.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible thin sheets made from rice are used in baking, so cookery sheets is a fair description.

clue.text: Badger is safe, protecting entrance to sett

indicators.note: the word for safe surrounds and guards the letter

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The badger is secure, guarding the way into its burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning nag.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag or harass them persistently.

clue.text: Wind in the Willows included seven tales orginally

indicators.note: originally (as printed, with a typo) means taking the original, first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A book about willows contained seven stories at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the book's title word (as in breeze) but is the verb, to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind something is to coil or turn it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Leading edge of Wild Wood scrub

indicators.note: the leading edge of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: The front of the Wild Wood is all scrubland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wild Wood is the menacing forest in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub something is to clean it, which is to wash it.

clue.text: Donkey and scruffy eagle stuffed by doctor for collection

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: the doctor's letters fill the rearranged bird
scruffy means messy, so the bird's letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB is the medical degree Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A taxidermist's collection: a donkey and a tatty eagle stuffed by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed by' suits taxidermy but means the doctor's letters fill the bird that 'scruffy' has scrambled into ELAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering or collection of things.

clue.text: Peep perhaps at families' waterside buildings

parts.note: Bo is the first name of Little Bo Peep of the nursery rhyme
noble families are houses, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Someone peeps at the families' boat sheds by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' signals that Peep is a surname defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheds for keeping boats stand by rivers and lakes, so they are waterside buildings.

clue.text: Shouty person circles town centre, becoming more jaundiced

indicators.note: the shouter's letters go round the others

parts.note: a yeller is someone who shouts

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A loud man prowls round the town centre, growing ever more bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice turns skin yellow, so someone more jaundiced looks yellower.

clue.text: Frolic in meadow quietly with sailor away from home

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
P is piano, the musical term for quietly
AB is an able-bodied seaman
out means not at home

explanation.surface: A sailor on leave romps quietly in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic is to romp, jump and play about.

clue.text: Party of snoopers from across The Pond sitting in the sun

indicators.note: the agency's letters sit inside the word for sun

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: American spies gatecrash a party, sunbathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering.

clue.text: Wife perched on stand for devious fellow

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter sits on top of the other word

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A wife sits atop a stand, scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, as in weaselly behaviour.

clue.text: Mole buys tea after ordering something to brew it in

indicators.note: once the letters are put in a new order they spell something else

parts.note: tea is brewed in a pot

explanation.surface: The Mole buys tea and then a pot to make it in.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole is the hero of The Wind in the Willows, but here a skin blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole on the face is a dark skin mark sometimes thought attractive, the beauty kind.

clue.text: Defence of messing about in boats

indicators.note: messing the letters about rearranges them

explanation.surface: Echoes Ratty's line that there is nothing like messing about in boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty famously says nothing is half so worth doing as messing about in boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a fortified projection, a stronghold of defence.

clue.text: Holy man and clueless daughter brought back those who'd lost their way

indicators.note: bringing back means turning the letters backwards

parts.note: ST is short for saint
naive means innocent, clueless

explanation.surface: A priest and a naive girl bring home some lost wanderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviants stray from accepted behaviour, people who have figuratively gone astray.

clue.text: Location coops up ten plucked hens — or half a dozen more?

indicators.note: the location encloses the numeral like hens in a coop

parts.note: a site is a location
X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: plucking removes the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A farm cooping ten scrawny hens wonders about adding six more.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the ten just mentioned: six more than ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten plus six makes the number, so half a dozen more than ten is right.

clue.text: Put upset girl in network of cells

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: to sit something is to put it down
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An upset girl is placed in a network of prison cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological tissue is a mass of similar cells working together.

clue.text: Foolish Toad wishes to be most mysterious

indicators.note: foolish suggests silly, disordered letters

explanation.surface: Toad, the vain hero of the Willows tale, foolishly wants an air of mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shadowy is obscure and mysterious, so the superlative means most mysterious.

clue.text: Old lizard twisted in exertion

indicators.note: twisting turns the letters round to read backwards
the letters lie inside the word exertion

explanation.surface: An ancient lizard wriggles with effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside exertion; 'twisted' reverses XERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannosaurus rex was a dinosaur, a prehistoric lizard by loose naming.

clue.text: Irritable spoilt child's head clipped with sides of tray

indicators.note: clipping the head removes the first letter

parts.note: a brat is a spoilt child

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cross brat has his hair cut and grabs the edges of a tray.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is also the Water Rat of The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered or irritable.

clue.text: See 19
Politicians are following the current figures

indicators.note: the politicians come after the current

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
Cons is short for Conservatives

explanation.surface: Politicians are tracking the latest numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are images or symbolic figures, as in religious figures.

clue.text: Small step led three oddly to discover compound

indicators.note: taking the odd letters, the 1st, 3rd, 5th and so on, across the words

explanation.surface: One small step led three people to a discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a chemical compound used in gunpowder.

clue.text: 30 Across arranged finalities of hare hunt. Nothing so far

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: the answer at 30 Across

indicators.note: the finalities of words are their last letters

explanation.surface: A hare hunt is set up but nothing has happened yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles STAYON into NOTASY; 'finalities of' adds the closing letters of hare and hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means not yet, up to now, so nothing has happened so far.

clue.text: Boy to traverse river? Don't go!

indicators.note: the boy spans across the river's letters

parts.note: a son is a boy
the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A boy is about to cross a river, and someone begs him to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to remain rather than leave is the plea in the exclamation.
